subject: Re: Performance SLO & context window follow-up (FinCo)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-18T15:12:00Z
Subject: Performance SLO recap + next steps

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery focused on performance requirements and context-window constraints so we have a clear mutual action plan. Main items from your side: 

- Target SLOs: p95 end-to-end latency <= 250ms (US region) for standard generation flows. Streaming behavior: first partial token should be available within ~1s of request start for interactive UIs.
- Throughput/Concurrency: steady-state throughput of ~40 requests/sec with spikes to 80r/s during batch campaigns; typical concurrent sessions expected between 16–32.
- Context window and token sizes: average input ~2,400 tokens, occasional long-context sessions up to 4,096 tokens; expected output size avg ~512 tokens, with peaks up to ~1,024 tokens.
- Other constraints: data retention & audit logs are standard but we flagged this for the security questionnaire follow-up.

What we proposed on the call:
1) Run a tailored benchmark using your sample prompt set (you mentioned you'll share) on both our hosted clusters and a Dedicated pool to measure p50/p95/p99 and streaming-first-chunk latency. Attached: a small baseline CSV with our internal 4k-context run so you can see the format.
2) Technical deep-dive with Rishi (solutions) + Neha (product) to align on dedicated sizing, batching/quantization tradeoffs, and fallback policies.
3) If benchmarks look good, we can scope a reserved capacity proposal and a short pilot (2–4 weeks) to validate in-prod behaviour.

Open questions we called out that I'll follow up on here:
- Do you need server-side or client-observed SLOs (network inclusion)? (We can report both.)
- Are strict streaming-first-chunk SLA numbers required for every request, or only interactive routes?
- Any regulatory constraints that would push you to Private deployment vs Dedicated?

Next steps: I'll run the baseline benchmarks with the sample prompts once you share them and loop Rishi in to schedule the deep-dive. Proposed times in my calendar: Tue/Wed next week afternoon ET — I can propose slots.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_latency_benchmarks_4096ctx.csv

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: finco-ml@finco.com
Date: 2026-07-19T09:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Performance SLO recap + next steps

Thanks Marissa — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side before you kick off the benchmark: 

1) When you call p95 end-to-end latency <= 250ms, is that server-side decode only or client-observed (i.e., includes our network)? For our SLA we need client-observed p95 <= 250ms in us-east.
2) Concurrency: our peak plan could go to sustained 32 concurrent sessions for the interactive product (each with a mix of 2.4k inputs and ~512 outputs). We can consider Dedicated if you recommend it for predictability — please include recommended target GPU counts and expected sustained rps.
3) Streaming: we require the first partial token to arrive within 1s for interactive sessions. After that, we expect steady streaming throughput. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports chunked streaming for long outputs (i.e., flush after first N tokens)?
4) Pricing impact: any rough delta in cost for supporting 4k context vs 2k (ballpark) — we need to assess economics for the pilot.

I've attached a ZIP of 20 representative prompts (finco_sample_prompts.zip). Happy to take the benchmark results — please include p50/p95/p99 and first-chunk latency.

Also — can we tentatively block Wed 2026-07-21 14:00 ET for the technical sync? I'll invite our infra lead if that works.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of ML Platform, FinCo
alex.johnson@finco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T16:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Performance SLO recap + next steps

Alex — great, thanks for the prompts and the clarifying questions. Quick answers inline: 

1) Latency definition: we can report both. Our internal benchmarking separates server-side decode (model + runtime) and client-observed (includes egress/network). For contractual SLAs we typically define p95 based on client-observed latency; we recommend adding a small network budget (we'll help quantify).

2) Concurrency & sizing: for sustained 32 concurrent interactive sessions with average inputs of ~2.4k and ~512 outputs, our recommendation is to run on Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool). On typical A100-class nodes we estimate that a Dedicated pool sized for 40 r/s sustained with headroom for spikes would require X nodes (we'll size precisely after the benchmark). If you want immediate predictability we can propose a conservative reservation for the pilot.

3) Streaming behavior: yes — Redwood supports chunked streaming (we flush partial tokens as they are generated). We instrument first-chunk latency separately; our baseline numbers show first-chunk under 500–700ms for many 4k-context runs on Dedicated hardware, but this depends on prompt structure and batch mixing. We'll capture first-chunk p50/p95 in the benchmark.

4) Cost delta for 4k vs 2k context: compute and memory scale non-linearly with input length. In practice you should expect ~1.5–2x higher GPU cost when moving a similar workload from 2k -> 4k context (depends on KV-cache hit rates and prompt distributions). We'll include model/quantization recommendations to optimize cost/quality tradeoffs.

Next steps:
- We've received finco_sample_prompts.zip — thanks. I'll run a bench on hosted + Dedicated-simulated pool and attach the results (CSV) here.
- Rishi / Neha: can you take ownership of a Dedicated-sizing run with 4k context + streaming enabled and capture these metrics: p50/p95/p99 server-side, first-chunk p50/p95, sustained rps at concurrency targets (16/32), memory utilization, and any quantization quality notes?
- Proposed tech sync: Wed 2026-07-21 14:00 ET works for us. I'll send a calendar invite and include a short agenda.

I'll send the benchmark CSV and a proposed reserved-capacity sketch by EOD Monday.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: proposed_technical_sync_agenda.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finco.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T10:05:00Z
Subject: Internal: Benchmark tasks for FinCo (4096 ctx + streaming)

Rishi / Neha — looping you in to own the benchmark work Marissa promised. Summary of asks from FinCo and what to capture during the run: 

- Inputs: use finco_sample_prompts.zip (20 representative prompts) + 100 synthetic variants to hit long-tail; run both: avg input ~2.4k tokens and stress cases at 4,096 tokens. Outputs avg ~512 tokens, with some up to 1,024.
- Metrics to capture (per-request and aggregate): server-side decode p50/p95/p99, client-observed p50/p95 (we'll simulate a small network budget), first-chunk latency p50/p95, sustained rps at concurrency 16 and 32, and memory/GPU utilization.
- Streaming: enable chunked streaming and measure time-to-first-byte and steady-state token throughput. Confirm that first-chunk < 1s client-observed (FinCo requires ~1s) and ideally first-chunk p95 < 1s.
- Cost/ops: run quantized and non-quantized variants; note quality regressions if any.

Deliverables: CSV with per-request rows (format like attached redwood_latency_benchmarks_4096ctx.csv), a short summary slide (one page) with recommended Dedicated sizing and expected monthly cost delta for 4k vs 2k, and a short list of follow-up risks (e.g., spike handling, long-tail tokens).

Timeline: can we have preliminary CSV by EOD Monday (2026-07-20) and a short summary before the Wed sync? Alex is joining the Wed 7/21 14:00 ET sync.

Thanks — please reply here with ownership and any blockers.

-Marissa
